\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Panel E: five-year averages aligned to 1981 (1981--1985 to 2016--2020), each period once; growth of real GDP per capita on government consumption (\% of GDP, WDI) G, G $\times$ ICRG/QoG, G $\times$ later period, G $\times$ ICRG/QoG $\times$ later period, ICRG/QoG, ICRG/QoG $\times$ later period, initial log GDP per capita, secondary enrolment and investment, with period effects. The windows of Table A14 (1981--2005 and 1996--2020) overlap in 1996--2005: in the main split the later period is 2006--2020; in the alternative split the overlap is assigned to the later period (1996--2020). FE: country and period fixed effects, wild cluster bootstrap by country (Webb weights, 9,999 replications) for the CI and p of the triple interaction. System GMM: specification of Table A14, panel A, with the added interactions instrumented like G $\times$ ICRG (lags 2 and deeper, collapsed), two-step, Windmeijer-corrected standard errors, normal 95\% CI. Interaction, early and late: G $\times$ ICRG/QoG in the earlier and in the later period. Panel F: government consumption / GDP replaced by an anchored synthetic series with no effect on growth, ln c\_sim,t = ln c\_obs,t$-$1 $-$ (1 $-$ ε\_it) Δln nominal GDP\_t + u\_t, with ε\_it = ε\_0 + ε\_1 $\times$ WGI\_i,t$-$1, ε\_0 = 0.556 and ε\_1 = $-$0.180 from the mechanism panel of this table (nominal growth of government consumption on nominal GDP growth $\times$ WGI, mean of the six indicators centred at its 1996--2023 mean, interpolated within country), and u drawn from the country's recentred values; the control sets the gradient to zero. 1,000 replications per design. Published specification: Table A14, panel D (Mollick and Vianna, 2024, GE, common sample of the three measures); approximate replication: Table A14, panel C. Share: simulated mean over the observed interaction; net share: (gradient mean $-$ control mean) over the observed interaction; shares are shown only for the same-year interaction, because the lagged and trend-GDP interactions are close to zero and their ratios are not meaningful. Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the second plan addendum).\end{minipage}
